chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Hamadhānī wrote to him: ʿAlī read to me the letter of your father regarding what he had made obligatory upon the owners of landed properties: that he obligates upon them half of one-sixth after expenses, and that whoever whose estate does not cover its own expenses is not liable for half of one-sixth nor anything else.

Those with us then differed concerning that, and they said: Khums is obligatory upon landed properties after expenses—meaning the expenses of the estate and its land tax, not the expenses of the man and his dependants.
So he wrote—and ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār read it: Khums is due on it after his expenses, the expenses of his dependants, and after the land tax of the ruler.

key_terms.الضِّيَاعِ: landed properties or estates that produce income
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth due as a religious financial obligation
key_terms.الْمَئُونَةِ: necessary expenses deducted before calculating khums
key_terms.خَرَاجِ السُّلْطَانِ: the ruler's land tax deducted before khums is due
key_terms.عِيَالِهِ: his dependants whose maintenance is included in deductible expenses
key_terms.نِصْفَ السُّدُسِ: half of one-sixth, referring to a reported earlier levy under discussion

ai.seo_question: Is khums on agricultural property calculated before or after personal and family expenses?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of khums on income from landed properties and clarifies a dispute over which expenses are deducted before khums is calculated. The ruling given is that khums is due only after personal expenses, the expenses of one's dependants, and the ruler's land tax have all been deducted.
